sentences.text: Judgment

The Writ Petition (Crl.) is filed seeking the following reliefs:
"i) To issue a writ in the nature of MANDAMUS or any other appropriate writ, order or direction compelling and commanding the respondents 1 and 2 to take investigation of the crime registered as 165/2018 of Mannarkkad Police Station.
ii) To issue a writ in the nature of MANDAMUS or any other appropriate writ, order or direction compelling and commanding the 1st respondent to constitute a special team of efficient, upright, incorrupt police officials to conduct the further investigation of the case.

sentences.text: The grievance of the petitioner is that there was no proper investigation in the suspicious death of his elder son, Sreejith.
According to the petitioner, his son was the part time sweeper of Karakkuzhi Service Co-operative Bank, Palakkad.
In 2025:KER:41387 2011, one Mr. N. Divakaran was the President and one Mr.Sherief was a director board member of the society.
They belongs to Indian National Congress which was the ruling party in the society.
According to the petitioner, his son was offered the post of peon in the society on condition that the petitioner will pay an amount of Rs. 6 Lakhs.
It is the case of the petitioner that, he could raise only Rs.3 lakhs, for giving the post of peon to his son.
It is the definite case of the petitioner that he gave the amount to the Director Board members.
The petitioner availed a loan of Rs.3 lakhs from the bank.

The petitioner gave the amount to five Director Board members namely, Divakaran, Ramkumar, Abboobaker Sidhique,
Vennamattom Thomas and Sherief is the submission.
On 05.12.2011, the payment was made directly to the above said persons in the society itself is the specific case of the petitioner.

Thereafter,
vacancies for the posts of Peon, Clerk etc. arose in the society, but Sreejith did not get any job.
The petitioner and his son was aggrieved by the same.

It is also the case of the petitioner that he made this issue as serious one and he made public the same and decided to take steps against 2025:KER:41387 the persons under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
At that time, the dead body of the petitioner's son was found in the tank of Maha Vishnu Temple at Pallikurippu.
The petitioner has serious doubt about the death of his son.
Hence this Writ petition is filed for issuing appropriate direction to respondents 1 and 2 to take investigation of the crime and do the needful in accordance with the law.

3. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, the learned Public Prosecutor and the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the Central Bureau of Investigation.
4. Counsel for the petitioner reiterated the contentions raised in this writ petition.
5. The Public Prosecutor submitted that three different officers investigated the matter and the officers were not able to find out any suspicion in the death and it was only an accidental death by drowning.

But the counsel for the petitioner submitted that, when the petitioner has a definite case that huge amount is accepted by the office bearers of the society as a bribe for getting job to his son,
and when his son did not get job, he 2025:KER:41387 either committed suicide or he might have been killed by somebody who apprehend that the petitioner will take steps under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
I do not want to make any observation about the same.
It is a fact that the petitioner lost his son.
He is aggrieved by the investigation conducted by the investigating agency.
According to the petitioner, he lost money by paying bribe to the office bearers of the society for getting a peon job for his son.
Whether there is any link between the death of the petitioner's son and the loss of his son's job is a matter to be investigated.
The Public Prosecutor submitted that a separate crime is registered under Section 420 IPC as far as the bribe issue is concerned.
Whether there is any link with that crime with the death of the petitioner's son is also to be looked into.
I do not want to make any further opinion about the same.

I am of the considered opinion that the District Police Chief,
Palakkad should call for the case diary and again peruse the same and decide whether further Narayanan M vs State Of Kerala on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55034845/
3 investigation is necessary.

sentences.text:
Therefore, this Writ Petition (Crl.) is disposed of in the following manner:
2025:KER:41387 1.

The 2nd respondent will call for the case diary in Crime No.165/2018 of Mannarkkad Police Station, Palakkad from the police station concerned and peruse the same and decide whether further investigation is necessary.
Before deciding the same, the 2 nd respondent will give an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner also.
2. If further investigation is necessary, the 2 nd respondent will do the needful forthwith.
The action taken by the 2 nd respondent will be communicated to the petitioner within six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
3. Petitioner will produce a certified copy of this judgment along with a copy of this writ petition (Crl.) with exhibits before the 2nd respondent for compliance.

Sd/-
